The Iran Ceasefire – Is Asia Getting Burned While Superpowers Play Chess?

My Asian brothers and sisters, the US-Iran ceasefire is holding by a thread, but look at the smoke it’s leaving behind for us in Asia! Oil prices spiked like a bush fire, Japan just pledged $10 billion to keep fuel flowing to Southeast Asia, and China is calling the truce “fragile” while denying it’s arming Iran. Meanwhile, our economies – from Bangkok markets to Manila ports – are choking on high energy costs. Is this the price we pay when big powers fight over the Strait of Hormuz? Should Asia form its own energy alliance instead of begging the West? Or is China the real stabiliser here, quietly pushing peace talks? Pakistan’s PM is flying around mediating – respect or just politics? Drop your hot take below: Who is winning, who is suffering, and what should ASEAN do next? Share if you feel the pinch at the pump! Tag your economist friends. What say you?
